# 02. Internal GO Calls

Source: 8/24/2026 GPC GO call before the Rush interview day (Grant, Eliza, Olivia), citation tag **[go]**; and 8/26/2026 GPC GO call opening the Delta Water Products engagement (Grant, Eliza Cuevas, Savannah Higgins, Olivia), citation tag **[delta-go]** = `transcripts/2026-08-26-delta-water-products/go-call-internal.md`. Other tags as defined in module 00.

Note on names: the GO call transcript spells the COO "Jodi" and the check-in transcript spells him "Jody." This playbook uses Jody. Nothing in the six 8/24 transcripts states his title outright, but the GO call refers to "AI tutoring with their COO last week" and the check-in refers to that same recorded one-on-one as Jody's, so COO is a strong reading rather than a stated fact **[inferred]**. The Delta contact renders as both "Madov" and "Madhav" in his own transcript; the playbook uses Madhav **[inferred]**.

## What a GO call is

The working definition, given while onboarding Olivia at the top of the Delta call: "go calls are kind of like the internal kickoff. Who's who in the zoo, what did we promise, what are we trying to do?" **[delta-go]** (Fathom splits that line across two speakers; best reading is Grant teaching, so the attribution is flagged **[inferred]**.)

Two configurations are now observed:

- **The pre-day huddle** (Rush, 8/24): short (18 minutes), held before a day of client-facing calls, focused on the day's politics, open loops, and deliverables.
- **The engagement opener** (Delta, 8/26): 26 minutes, held before *any* client-facing call on a new engagement, focused on transferring context from the sales seat to the consulting seat, scoping risk, and process setup.

Both do the same five jobs; the engagement opener adds jobs of its own, below.

## The five jobs of a GO call

1. **Read the client's emotional and political state.** On 8/24: negative kickoff feedback, a COO who "was not impressed by the first tutoring session," and a sponsor whose real stake is job security — "it is owning and making sure that they don't get seen as a [word dropped by the transcript]. It's like they need, it's job security." **[go]** On 8/26 the same job runs for a brand-new client: Larry (platform president) is the executive sponsor and "he likes us"; Madhav, unexpectedly, is the signatory ("I was not expecting him to be the signatory") and reads as head of BI; the department heads are "curious, slightly skeptical about who we are and what we can accomplish. It's not all happy-go-lucky vibes... They're bought in, which is good." **[delta-go]** Know whose neck is on the line and who holds the pen before anyone gets interviewed.
2. **Own misses out loud.** 8/24: "We got negative feedback on the kickoff call, which I will own for trying to rush that into a half hour. Lesson learned." **[go]** 8/26, the same reflex applied to a scoping miss: a 10-hour SOW signed against a whole portfolio — "we may have put ourselves in a disadvantage because we didn't sign off on that at the beginning, but it doesn't mean that we can't claw out of that one." **[delta-go]** Mistakes convert to plans, fast, without drama.
3. **List the open loops.** 8/24: governance and the security path, Claude access, Lacy's demeanor, the Jody asset, the domain migration, payment status. **[go]** 8/26: the unanswered focus-brand question, the onboarding form status (checked live on the call), the un-templated kickoff SOP, the unbuilt account-scaffold step. **[delta-go]** An open loop that isn't named on the GO call gets dropped during the engagement.
4. **Define deliverables in countable terms.** 8/24: two workflow demos plus the Jody spreadsheet asset, which deliberately doesn't count toward the two. **[go]** 8/26 counts in hours instead: the Gold Workflow Assessment template at "36.25" hours — "And not a cent over" — with time tracked against it (see instrumentation, below). **[delta-go]**
5. **Set the communication cadence.** 8/24: weekly check-ins, Monday recap emails, demo live on calls instead of iterating over email. **[go]** 8/26: the pre-kickoff email to Madhav (introduce Olivia, ask the focus-brand question), interview scheduling structure designed before the client asks (Olivia proposing Monday–Thursday blocks, "two, three hour blocks with a break in the middle"), and interview days pinned to Monday–Wednesday of kickoff week. **[delta-go]**

## What the engagement opener adds

Observed once, on the Delta call — treat as first sketch until a second engagement opener lands.

- **The seat handoff is explicit.** "I'm currently in the sales seat and I'm wearing my kind of executive hat, transferring information over to a... workflow consultant." **[delta-go]** The transfer is graduated and stated in ratios: "those [Rush] calls, I'd like us to be more like 50-50... And then in the Delta situation, I would like you to be taking more of a lead." A handoff nobody names is a handoff that doesn't happen.
- **Scope risk gets named before the client feels it.** The portfolio math said the SOW couldn't work: "that is 10 hours spread across four different finance departments and two marketing departments... it's just not going to go well." The fix is focus — "If we try to go for everything, we're not going to get anything done" — and the focus question is handed to the client as a reflective exercise: "Which brand in the portfolio do you think we should go after? And just put them in the reflective seat before we have our kickoff call." **[delta-go]**
- **Land one, multiply later.** The one-brand focus is also the revenue architecture, cross-referenced to the sister engagement the way RubyPlay was on 8/24: "just like we're seeing with Freeman, this is a dream scenario where one portfolio, one CFO, one president to convince, but multiple retainers... every brand should get their own workflow assessment." **[delta-go]**
- **Read the client's self-assessment skeptically but respectfully.** Delta's boardroom produced "like 93 different opportunities" with timelines "completely out of whack, like not rooted in anything justifiable" — and one hard fact worth its weight: asked whether they trust their HubSpot data, "they said flat out, no." **[delta-go]** The enthusiasm is real, the sizing isn't; both facts shape the engagement.
- **Prep the kickoff's one sentence.** The kickoff (module 05, sourced from the 8/19 Rush Leadership Kickoff as of v0.6; the earlier note that no kickoff transcript existed is superseded) gets its target set here: "I always like to try to get one engagement-defining statement for the entire first project... And we want them to say yes." And the collection goal: "The goal of the kickoff call is to get as many quotes as possible as to how you're going to judge us. So we want to use those quotes over and over again." **[delta-go]**
- **The onboarding form gates the kickoff — flexibly.** The closed-won automation creates the folder and sends the form (pain points, KPIs, minimum definition of success). Enforcement scales with client size: "if they're smaller and we can boss them around... go fill out the form. When it's a publicly traded company, I'm going to give them a pass." **[delta-go]** (Fathom scatters this exchange across speakers; the posture is Grant's **[inferred]**.)

## Patterns worth copying

- **Prep the asset before the meeting where it matters.** Olivia, on the Jody asset: "the fix for it is almost there. I'm just testing it in all three models to make sure that they're giving consistent results, and it'll be done before our call with Lacy." **[go]** Observed once; whether cross-model testing becomes standing practice is a team decision **[inferred]**.
- **Reference the sister engagement.** RubyPlay as template and cautionary tale on 8/24 ("RubyPlay is the taster of what Rush is going to look like" / "I did not do my best on RubyPlay") **[go]**; Freeman as the portfolio playbook on 8/26 **[delta-go]**. Every engagement teaches the next one, and the GO call is where that transfer happens.
- **Flag environment variance.** Olivia: "the hard part is that we just don't know what settings are set up in Claude or in [ChatGPT]." Grant: "if they have memory turn on... all those things affect outcomes. So, that's the hard part when you're using a prompt and not a skill." **[go]** When you can't control the client's environment, say so early and push toward skills over prompts.
- **Keep money on the agenda.** Eliza raised payment on 8/24 ("have we received payment from Rush?") **[go]** and again on 8/26 ("Did we invoice them already?"), which opened a full receivables review — Delta, Rush, RubyPlay, Joy, Ballsteel, Future Holidays, and Crank Tank all outstanding, with Savannah owning follow-up. **[delta-go]** Grant's framing: "It's a good problem to have, to have people owe us money, but it's a better problem to... know where to spend it, when it's actually in our bank account." Consultants who never check receivables become consultants who work for free.
- **Instrument the process while running it.** The Gold Workflow Assessment template gets its first live test on Rush and Delta, and the GO call assigns the measurement: "Olivia, we redid all the structure of the workflow assessment... it's the first time it's really going to get tested... we want to know what's the happy path, what's the common thread," with Grant pre-registering his own prediction ("For the record, I do believe that we are going to have more hours consumed") and Savannah's rule: "We just need to know where they're being consumed. So make sure you're tracking appropriately." **[delta-go]** Estimates are hypotheses; engagements are the experiments.
- **Train by having the trainee produce the artifact.** Rather than writing the kickoff template himself: "Let's get the call... recording of Rush over to Olivia and have Olivia fill out the form." **[delta-go]** The SOP gets updated and the new consultant learns the call in one move.
- **Continuity lives in the repo.** "All of the discovery calls will need to be inside of the GitHub repo to make sure that there's continuity." **[delta-go]** Client account scaffolding (repo creation and loading) is itself a skill step in ClickUp — flagged on the call as not yet fully built.
